lines.text: Four years ago, NASA crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid. Now Europe is back to inspect the damage.
In 2022, NASA's DART probe slammed into Dimorphos, a tiny moon that circles the asteroid Didymos.
That hit shortened the moon's orbit by about 32 minutes. A real test of planetary defence.
Now ESA's Hera spacecraft has sent its first close-up of both asteroids, from about 60 kilometres away.
And it shows a side of Didymos that DART never got to see.
Boulders, craters, and strange grooves or ridges. Some may be debris thrown over from the crash.
Didymos is about 780 metres wide. Its little moon? Only about 150.
Next, Hera moves in closer for a full crash-site investigation, so we learn how to protect Earth.
